knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly. A compression marker whose second colon sits on the
delimiter kept just past the address span is accepted as well.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling: cecb3df teaches knownhost_parse_ipv6 that `end` is an exclusive bound on the address body but that callers keep one delimiter byte immediately after it, and it reads that byte (p <= end) to accept a '::' whose second colon sits on the delimiter. At that commit every caller passes a pointer into a NUL-terminated host (or a bracketed token whose next byte is ']'), so the extra read is in-bounds and ordinary literals never reach it. d476829 then parses from a private allocation of exactly address_len bytes, so a bracket, port, or comma following the token cannot be consumed as part of the literal. That copy is correct for a length-bounded parser, and by itself the original p < end check never touches the byte past the copy. Only together do they overflow: a known-hosts hostname that ends on a single colon (in-contract text, not a finished IPv6 literal) makes the parser dereference the delimiter while the buffer no longer contains one. Restoring p < end makes the copy safe; allocating the delimiter byte makes the peek safe. Either edit alone leaves the check path clean, so the repair has to reconcile the delimiter contract in the parser with the exact-sized span introduced later.
